title: Cornerstone harvest — long-context quicknotes & synthesis
content:
Purpose: rapid, messy brain dump after two days reading + hallway convos at ContextSummit. Collect heuristics we might actually ship as small flags in the runtime to improve long-session quality without blowing cost or latency.

High-level takeaways: 
- Users expect "coherent state" across very long sessions (~10k+ tokens) but we can't keep full KV for everything. Need selective retention + cheap re-anchoring.
- Two practical levers: (A) token-level salience scoring + decay; (B) episodic checkpoints (compressed prefix snapshots) for warm-starts.

Open heuristics to test (prioritized):
1) Prefix trim with salience threshold: walk prefix from oldest->newest, compute simple salience score (tf-like with recency boost). Evict until total retained tokens <= budget. Quick metric: coherence-drop-on-core-prompts (use existing eval set).
2) Anchor markers: when user issues an explicit "save" intent (explicit or implicit via high-divider tokens), snapshot compressed embedding of context window, store as cheap checkpoint; when retrieval hits lower quality, inject checkpoint instead of raw KV.
3) Sparse bloom filter for entity mentions: keep detailed KV for most mentioned entities, purge low-frequency context. 
4) Byte budget per conversation: enforce soft budget, but allow N most recent tokens always. Track per-user budget and degrade gracefully by swapping to smaller quantized model for old history.

Experiment sketches: 
- Light eval: sample 200 real session transcripts (internal anon set), simulate eviction policies, compute reranked answer BLEU/EM and token-cost delta.
- Ablations: salience-only vs recency-only vs salience+checkpoint. Also try checkpoint compression with product quantization vs avg-embedding compression.

Immediate TODOs: 
- [ ] assemble 200 sessions and sanitize PII (ask DataSec for one-off access)
- [ ] prototype salience scorer (fast counts + position decay) as Python stub (ramon/salience-stub)
- [ ] run cost vs coherence sweep and plot knee point (latency & tokens retained)

Risks & questions: 
- Checkpoint injection might cause sudden topic jumps; need marker for model to know "this is compressed snapshot, not verbatim" — include synthetic bridging sentence when injecting.
- How to measure "coherence" cheaply? Candidate: task-based QA on curated highlights + human soft scores for 50 sessions.

Notes from talks: 
- Dr. Nguyen: "kernels are fast enough, state movement is the cost" -> prioritize reducing KV movement frequency.
- Panel: small quantization error often beats expensive cache lookups for old context. Good to test mixed-precision fallback.

Brain fuzz ideas (one-liners):
- Maintain two caches: hot KV (full precision) + cold compressed checkpoint list with timestamps. If cold checkpoint used, prepend one-line summary generated when checkpoint created.
- Use query-time local attention to stitch checkpoint-inserted summary into current attention window with a small adapter layer.

Quick sketch (ASCII):
[recent tokens] ----- HOT KV ----- (keep N recent tokens)
[older span] -- checkpoint_42 (compressed summary + embedding) -- [even older spans purged]

References I want to read next: 
- paper on episodic memory compression (arXiv link above)
- retrieval-augmented conversation QoE studies (conference notes folder)

If you see this and want to riff: leave a short note in the GH PR linked above or ping me in slack. Will iterate into a short proposal for runtime flags if early sims look promising.

-- Ramon
